item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-bb1d46b01b28eb25","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"In Germany, 260,100 dwellings were approved for construction in 2023, 26.6% fewer than in 2022 and the lowest level since 2012; Destatis attributed some of the decline to higher material costs and worse financing conditions.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns Germany in 2023; the source reports an outcome and possible contributing conditions, not direct causal attribution to Scholz.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect: the result occurred during Scholz's chancellorship, but the source does not identify a specific Scholz decision as the cause.","limitations":["Building approvals are a leading indicator of future activity, not completed construction.","The source gives multiple possible causes rather than a government-specific causal finding."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bb1d46b01b28eb25","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Housing approvals for new buildings fell by 29.7% in 2023; approvals initiated by private persons fell 42.2%, company applications fell 20.3%, and approvals for publicly initiated applications fell 12.1%.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns Germany in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect: the outcome occurred under the federal government led by Scholz, without a specific attribution in the source.","limitations":["Approval data do not establish actual housing completions or distributional effects.","The source does not isolate federal from private, state, or municipal responsibility."]},{"source_id":"SRC-bb1d46b01b28eb25","start_unit":5,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Approvals for new apartments in multifamily buildings fell 25.1% in 2023 to 142,600, while approvals for single-family and two-family homes fell 39.1% and 48.3%, respectively.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns Germany in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect: the source reports a national housing-market outcome during Scholz's term but does not attribute it to his personal decisions.","limitations":["The measure is planned construction, not completed housing or actual affordability.","No direct federal policy mechanism is identified."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b426e4d2373273c4","start_unit":2,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In a March 2023 CNN interview after meeting President Biden, Scholz said Western support for Ukraine was united, reaffirmed continuing financial, humanitarian, and weapons assistance, and stated that Germany had spent €14 billion on Ukraine-related support in the previous year.","question_ids":["2B.5","2B.8","2B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns Scholz's public position and German policy in March 2023; the cited €14 billion refers to the preceding year.","ruler_attribution":"Direct: Scholz made the statements and described the government's support policy.","limitations":["The source does not independently verify the €14 billion figure or assess the legality, proportionality, or effects of each measure.","The article records stated policy and reported spending, not complete execution records."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b426e4d2373273c4","start_unit":3,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"Scholz said negotiations to end the Ukraine war should begin only when Putin understood he could not win and had to withdraw Russian troops; he also said Germany and its partners would not decide territorial issues on Ukraine's behalf.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","2B.10","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly concerns Scholz's stated position in March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Direct: the position was stated by Scholz in an interview.","limitations":["This is a public negotiating position, not evidence of an implemented peace agreement or settlement.","The source does not assess whether the position increased or reduced the probability of negotiations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b426e4d2373273c4","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Scholz said Germany had reduced dependence on Russian gas, coal, and oil by increasing LNG imports from Western Europe, building new northern German LNG terminals, and extending nuclear-plant operating periods; he stated that Germany had avoided a gas shortage and economic crisis.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns measures and claimed conditions reported in March 2023, with some actions extending from 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct: Scholz described these as government actions and outcomes during his chancellorship.","limitations":["The claim that no economic crisis occurred is Scholz's statement in the article, not an independent evaluation.","The source does not quantify costs, environmental effects, or longer-term energy-security consequences."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b426e4d2373273c4","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Scholz said Germany had asked China not to supply weapons to Russia and expressed optimism that the request would succeed.","question_ids":["1B.6","2B.5","2B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns Scholz's diplomatic action and expectation in March 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Direct: Scholz reported making the request.","limitations":["The source provides no evidence that China complied or that the request was backed by an enforceable control mechanism."]},{"source_id":"SRC-2e4094c1066142aa","start_unit":6,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"The German government participated in the June 2023 Ukraine Recovery Conference in London, with the stated aim of mobilizing international support for Ukraine's economic and social stabilization and reconstruction; the government highlighted humanitarian aid, reconstruction financing, infrastructure repair, investment guarantees, domestic reforms, and an EU-accession perspective.","question_ids":["2B.5","2B.7","2B.10","5B.1","5B.4","5B.6","6B.6","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns German government participation and stated policy in June 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect: the source describes federal-government policy and ministerial participation, but does not attribute the measures personally to Scholz.","limitations":["The source is an official government account and does not quantify German disbursements or independently evaluate implementation.","The named participants were Baerbock and Schulze rather than Scholz."]},{"source_id":"SRC-d361b8f62667024f","start_unit":5,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"At the May 2023 Global Solutions Summit, Scholz called for an international order based on the UN Charter and international law and suggested a more inclusive and balanced order; at the Council of Europe summit he emphasized the rule of law, democracy, the European Court of Human Rights, support for Ukraine, reconstruction, and judicial capacity development.","question_ids":["2B.7","2B.10","3B.4","4B.4","8B.1","8B.9"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns Scholz's speeches and diplomatic activity in May 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Direct: the statements and proposed priorities are attributed to Scholz.","limitations":["The source records rhetoric and participation, not completed institutional reforms or measurable outcomes.","The page is an official government presentation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c0ea19b65580cd21","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"In August 2023, the Institut der deutschen Wirtschaft forecast that Germany's real GDP would fall by nearly 0.5% in 2023, average inflation would be about 6.5%, investment in construction would fall 3%, and average unemployment would rise by about 160,000 to an unemployment rate of 5.5%.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"A contemporaneous August 2023 forecast for Germany's 2023 economic performance.","ruler_attribution":"No direct attribution: the institute identified weak external demand, high interest rates, expensive energy, and global conditions; it called for government action but did not assign responsibility for the forecast outcomes to Scholz.","limitations":["These were forecasts rather than final outcomes.","The institute recommended lower tax burdens and less bureaucratic innovation and investment support, but the source does not establish whether Scholz adopted them."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c4d1b1e780fb6b4d","start_unit":7,"end_unit":9,"fact_summary":"A first Destatis estimate reported that German GDP fell 0.3% in 2023; the first quarter grew 0.1% quarter-on-quarter, the second and third quarters stagnated, and the fourth quarter contracted 0.3%. The article linked weakness to global conditions, high inflation and interest rates, the war in Ukraine, and the November 2023 constitutional-court budget ruling, which reduced available government funding.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.6","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7","8B.8","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns Germany's 2023 economic performance and the late-2023 budget constraint.","ruler_attribution":"Mixed and indirect: the source identifies external shocks and a court ruling as important factors, while reporting that the budget ruling constrained the coalition's spending and investment options.","limitations":["The GDP figure was a first estimate and later revisions may differ.","The article is not a causal evaluation of Scholz's policies."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f7c7d69225ebb851","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"In 2023, 17.7 million people in Germany, or 21.2% of the population, were at risk of poverty or social exclusion, nearly unchanged from 21.1% in 2022; 14.3% were at risk of poverty, 6.9% experienced severe material and social deprivation, and 9.8% of people under 65 lived in households with very low work intensity.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Directly concerns Germany in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Indirect: the indicators describe social conditions during Scholz's chancellorship but do not identify which government policies caused them.","limitations":["The figures are first results and the income questions refer to the prior year's income.","EU-SILC methodology changed in 2020, preventing direct comparison with earlier years."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c457864428e8b585","start_unit":7,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"In a December 2023 decision, the Federal Constitutional Court held that an injunction barring a company from reporting allegations of sexualized violence had been suspended because of an obvious violation of procedural equality of arms; it treated the constitutional complaint's prospects of success as obvious and ordered full reimbursement of the complainant's necessary expenses.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.8","4B.3","4B.4","4B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly concerns a German constitutional-court decision issued in December 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Institutional/contextual only: the finding concerns the independent constitutional court and a Berlin court order, not a personal Scholz decision.","limitations":["The case does not evaluate the federal chancellor or federal government.","It concerns an individual proceeding and cannot by itself establish broader institutional performance."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-5aa7082f6d5d50e9","SRC-57b870e856fe0484","SRC-6ff341f0e9342750","SRC-2fb3ef32d73055e1"],"batch_limitations":["Several documents concern Germany-wide outcomes or institutional actions without identifying a specific Scholz decision; attribution is therefore indirect or contextual.","The supplied documents provide limited direct evidence for nuclear risk, domestic violence, corruption, personal integrity, appointments, surveillance, and social-service implementation during 2023.","Documents with later publication or reference periods were not used as evidence for the 2023-2023 ruler period."]}
